The final answer q = 2 matches my recollection of the known result, but the supporting argument is flawed, so I could not confirm the answer from the argument itself.

**Where the argument fails.** The solution claims that on ℤ a finite p-th moment with 1 < p < 2 makes the sandpile explode, while a finite mean alone keeps it stable. These two claims are inconsistent with each other. On ℤ, i.i.d. masses with mean μ < 1 and a finite mean already stabilize. This is the standard one-dimensional case, so ℤ cannot be the worst-case graph.

The heuristic odometer sum Σ_d V(d)^{1−p} is also not justified. The step "flux spread evenly over V′(d) vertices, then multiply by V′(d)" is only a rough scaling guess. In addition, the inequality V(d) ≥ d would make linear-growth graphs the worst case, which contradicts the known behavior of ℤ.

**The answer itself.** As I recall, the published result is that finite p-th moments with p > 2 guarantee stabilization on every bounded-degree graph, and for p < 2 there are bounded-degree graphs with explosion. Those graphs are not ℤ. That matches q = 2, though I am relying on memory and did not derive it.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
